props.gloss_en: 'let the waters swarm... and birds fly' (Gen 1:20) -- apparently birds were created from water
'and from the ground the Lord God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the sky' (Gen 2:19) -- apparently birds were created from land
birds were created from the mud
birds were created from the water
why did He bring them to Adam? to give them names
a bird has no [requirement of] slaughter from the Torah
as it is said 'and he shall spill' (Lev 17:13) -- mere spilling suffices
the slaughter of a bird is from the Torah (the position R' Yitzchak ben Pinchas and R' Elazar HaKappar deny, and the stam reports of Rebbi at 28a.5)
[the undomesticated animal] is juxtaposed to disqualified consecrated animals
the bird is juxtaposed to the animal, as it is written 'this is the law of the animal and the bird' (Lev 11:46)
the mishna (85a): one who slaughters and it became a carcass in his hand, one who stabs and one who rips -- is exempt from covering
do you think [the mishna speaks] of a bird? no -- of an undomesticated animal
one who slaughters and needs the blood is obligated to cover; how does he act? he either stabs it or rips it
no -- [the baraita speaks] of an undomesticated animal whose blood he needs for dye
if he pinched [the neck of a bird-offering] with a knife, it renders garments impure [when it is] in the throat
he [R' Yitzchak ben Pinchas] said it in accordance with this tanna
as disqualified consecrated animals are [permitted] by slaughter, so the gazelle and the deer are by slaughter
and a bird has no slaughter by the words of the Torah, but by the words of the scribes
'and you shall slaughter... as I commanded you' (Deut 12:21) teaches that Moses was commanded on the gullet and the windpipe, on the majority of one in a bird and the majority of two in an animal
